predecessors.name: Omani Empire (East African coast)
predecessors.text: the African section of the Omani Empire, 'ruled by Majid bin Said' after the division of 19 October 1856

successors.name: British Colonial Empire
successors.text: Zanzibar itself, which 'became a British protectorate' under the Heligoland-Zanzibar Treaty of 1 July 1890

successors.name: German Africa
successors.text: the Sultan's mainland coast within what became German East Africa (Cliopatria's 1888 shape cut by the Tanganyika mainland; the pages give no line)

successors.name: Imperial British East Africa Company
successors.text: Mombasa, relinquished on 25 May 1887 to the British East Africa Association, later the Imperial British East Africa Company

ledger.x: 19 October 1856: Majid bin Said becomes the first Sultan of Zanzibar.
1856: the Banadir coast is allotted to Zanzibar.
25 May 1887: Mombasa is relinquished to the British East Africa Association.
28 April 1888: Sultan Khalifah bin Said signs the coast over to the German East Africa Company.
1 July 1890: Zanzibar becomes a British protectorate.

wars.name: Abushiri revolt
wars.outcome: German East Africa Company administration of the coast set off a revolt in 1888; Abushiri was 'captured and executed on 15 December 1889' and the German government took control on 1 January 1891.

certainty.note: No line is given by the pages: the Sultan's dominion is a coastal strip and its claims ('Until 1884 ... a substantial portion of the Swahili Coast').
